Firms whose revenue is small relative to the sum of their plant and acquired intangible assets have accumulated capital that the business does not use, and that idle or overpriced base is progressively written down or earns below its cost.
considered.reasoning:
Rather than re-running the champion with a different aggregation operator, this asks a decomposition-style question directly: the archive's Low CROIC result showed that *cash* generated per dollar of invested capital predicts returns, and this substitutes revenue for cash to identify whether the effect is about capital that produces no business at all or specifically about cash conversion. It is a single-ratio construct with no rank product, so its slope cannot be attributed to a coverage or profitability leg's main effect, and coverage should be high because sales, plant, and intangibles are broadly reported.
REASONING_END: n/a
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Heavy Investment With High Cash Return on Capital
considered.hypothesis: The positive half of the task's economic story is that aggressive investment is value-creating when the firm has demonstrated it can earn cash on the capital it already owns. Firms combining a high capital-spending rate with a high cash return on gross invested capital are compounding a proven franchise, while equally aggressive investors earning poor returns on existing capital are destroying value.
considered.reasoning:
The archive's short side has repeatedly shown that heavy investment is punished when cash generation is weak, but the symmetric proposition — that heavy investment is *rewarded* when demonstrated returns on capital are high — has never been tested with the cash-return-on-invested-capital measure that proved to be the most informative quality gauge here. The two legs use different capital bases (net plant for the spending rate, gross plant plus intangibles for the return), so neither leg mechanically drives the other, and both are bounded ranks so the long tail is populated by genuinely high-return expanders.
REASONING_END: n/a
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Purchased Base With Accrual-Driven Earnings
considered.hypothesis: Acquirers under pressure to show that a deal worked can report earnings that cash flow does not support. A heavy purchased-intangible load per revenue dollar combined with persistently positive accruals — earnings systematically exceeding operating cash flow — identifies firms whose acquisition thesis is being sustained on paper, and both the earnings and the carrying value are subsequently reversed.
considered.reasoning: This is the one major quality dimension never paired with the champion's investment leg: accrual reliability, measured as a three-year average earnings-minus-cash-flow gap so that single-year working-capital swings do not drive it. It is economically distinct from every conditioner tested in this family — coverage, liquidity, maturity, cumulative profits, productivity — because a firm can have ample cash coverage and still be reporting earnings its cash flow does not support, and the interaction claim is that accrual aggressiveness is diagnostic specifically for acquisition-heavy balance sheets.

considered.name: Sub-Replacement Spending With Claims Well Covered
considered.hypothesis: Spending persistently below the replacement rate implied by depreciation is capital discipline when the firm's cash flow comfortably covers its obligations — it is a deliberate harvest of a mature asset base with cash returned rather than reinvested — and is capacity starvation when it is not. The disciplined version is underpriced because depreciation-heavy accounting makes these firms look tired.
considered.reasoning: The gen-8 finding that capacity liquidation relative to obligations predicted *higher* returns (slope +2.77 against a negative prediction) says under-investment is rewarded and that the correct specification separates disciplined harvesters from starved firms using the conditioner that has carried both slope and alpha throughout this archive. It differs from the earlier harvest signals, which used asset age or cash-flow-to-assets and produced alphas of only 1–2%, by identifying the harvest through the *flow* decision (capex versus depreciation) and the strength through obligation coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Acquisitions Funded With New Long-Term Debt
considered.hypothesis: The financing of an acquisition determines who bears the cost of overpayment. Firms making large acquisitions while simultaneously adding long-term debt have levered the purchase price onto the equity claim, so any shortfall in the acquired business is amplified into impairment, covenant pressure, and forced divestiture.
considered.reasoning: Every acquisition-related signal in this archive conditions on the *adequacy* of cash flow; none conditions on the *source of funds* for the purchase itself, which is a separable economic channel — an acquirer paying from surplus cash and one issuing debt look identical on a coverage screen in the deal year. Both legs are contemporaneous flows measuring one decision, and scaling new long-term debt by the existing liability stock makes the leg a measure of how much the firm's claim structure was expanded to buy growth rather than a size effect.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Purchased Base Per Dollar of Gross Profit
considered.hypothesis: What justifies an acquisition price is the earnings power it brings, not the revenue. Measuring the purchased intangible base against three-year average gross profit gives the number of years of the acquired business's actual margin needed to recover what was paid; when that payback horizon is long, the price cannot be earned back and impairment follows.
considered.reasoning:
The incoherent asset-plus-claims denominator is gone: this is a clean payback horizon in which the investment stock is divided by the quality flow that must service it, and gross profit is positive for essentially all firms so there is no sign inversion. It is economically distinct from the champion's intangibles-per-sales leg because it prices the acquired revenue at the margin actually earned — paying two times sales for a 60%-margin business and for a 10%-margin business are entirely different decisions that the revenue-scaled measure treats identically.
REASONING_END: n/a
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Growth With Habitual Self-Funding
considered.hypothesis: What validates expansion is not the size of one window's cash surplus but whether the firm routinely covers its capital spending out of operations. Counting how many of the past five years had operating cash flow above capital expenditure identifies habitual self-funders, and capacity growth by such firms reflects an internally imposed hurdle rather than access to accommodating capital markets.
considered.reasoning:
This replaces a deflator swap with a different functional form of the conditioner — a persistence count rather than a scaled cumulative difference — so it is not a monotone transformation of the tested asset-scaled surplus measure: a firm with one huge surplus year and four deficit years scores low here and high there. The count is also robust to lumpy investment and to scale, and it makes the economic claim explicit, namely that financing discipline is a habit that distinguishes productive from opportunistic growth.
REASONING_END: n/a
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Purchased Growth Without Earned Capital
considered.hypothesis: A firm that has accumulated no retained earnings has never demonstrated that it can earn a return on capital; when such a firm's balance sheet also carries a heavy load of purchased intangible capital per revenue dollar, its growth has been bought with outside money by management with no track record of internal value creation, and the acquired base is the most likely place for that inexperience to be revealed.
considered.reasoning:
This repairs the archive's earliest diagnosed failure rather than ensembling two winners: the retained-earnings life-cycle conditioner produced the strongest cross-sectional slope in the entire search (fmb −3.33) but no tradable alpha, and the diagnosis was that its investment leg — acquisition flow with a large exact-zero mass — could not form a stable extreme portfolio. Pairing that conditioner with the continuously distributed intangible-load leg tests the diagnosis directly, and the conditioner is economically independent of the cash-coverage and liquidity channels that dominate the rest of the archive because it measures cumulative earned capital rather than current cash adequacy.
REASONING_END: n/a

critic_notes.rationale: This is a difference of two long-published anomaly ranks (Cooper-Gulen-Schill asset growth and cash-based operating profitability) with no genuine conditioning — an additive composite whose loadings are already spanned by standard investment and profitability factors.

The construction is sound (a strictly positive [0,1] rank multiplier scales the asset-growth slope without flipping its sign, so the expected negative sign is coherent), and volatility-conditioned investment is a defensible refinement, though the reasoning text misstates the direction ("most negative for high-growth/high-vol" when such firms in fact score most positive) and the signal remains largely a rescaled asset-growth exposure.

This is a direct rediscovery of the net external financing anomaly (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan) and the debt-issuance anomaly, and worse, the two legs are near-mechanical duplicates since a capex-minus-cash-flow deficit is by the funding identity plugged with debt or equity, so SUMRANK double-counts one construct rather than requiring independent confirmation.

The economic story is interesting and non-obvious, but multiplying two signed z-scores makes the negative-by-negative quadrant (low capex, deteriorating margins) score just as high as the intended high-capex/improving-margin quadrant, so the expression does not compute the productive-versus-unproductive investment split the hypothesis describes and the reasoning ignores this quadrant entirely.

Both legs are bounded [0,1] ranks so the product cleanly isolates the intended joint corner with the correct negative sign, and the acquisitive-growth × low-retained-earnings life-cycle interaction is a substantively distinct construct rather than a restatement of asset growth — the main caveat is the large mass of exact-zero acquirers created by COALESCE, which will make the low end of the first rank leg a degenerate tie block worth checking in the coverage and turnover diagnostics.

Both legs are canonical published anomalies (Thomas-Zhang inventory growth and Sloan accruals) and they are mechanically overlapping, since the inventory change is itself a component of the working-capital accrual measured by ib−oancf, so the "interaction" largely re-multiplies one accounting construct by itself.

The expression matches the hypothesis and the sign is coherent, but the two legs are mechanically linked (headcount growth is the denominator driving sales-per-employee down), so the interaction risks collapsing into a re-expression of the well-known hiring-rate anomaly rather than an independent conditioning variable.

This is a double-sort of two of the most heavily published anomalies—net share issuance and profitability/ROA—each of which already predicts returns with the stated sign, so the product is likely to rediscover their union rather than isolate any genuine conditional effect.

Construction is internally consistent (both legs bounded in [0,1], product monotone in the predicted negative direction) and the industry-ranked capex leg is a sensible fix, though "investment intensity punished under financial constraint/distress" is a familiar theme and the oancf/lt coverage window will limit sample breadth.

critic_notes.target_name: Inventory Wedge Scaled by Margin Cushion
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archive's "Inventory Buildup at Thin Margins" with the investment leg's rank swapped for a winsorized z-score—a transformation-only change of exactly the cosmetic-variant type the objective warns against—and it also silently converts a one-corner conditional into a signed monotone signal without acknowledging that the negative-wedge half is now an active long leg.

The mechanism (unverified purchased intangibles plus weak cash earnings as impairment risk) is coherent and the expression matches it, but the stated advantage over the acquisitive-growth signal is contradicted by the construction: COALESCE(intan,0) reintroduces exactly the degenerate zero-tie block the reasoning claims to avoid, and the cash-flow leg alone is close to a known profitability sort.

Beyond being a denominator swap on the gen-0 margin-validated capex template, ppent appears in both legs, so heavy investors mechanically depress sales-to-capital during the buildout phase—the interaction is partly an accounting artifact rather than the intended utilization test.

This is a cosmetic denominator swap on the already-evaluated "Capex Without Debt-Service Capacity" (identical IND_RANK(capx/ppent) leg, lt→lct plus a cash term in the same negated coverage rank), and since che/lct and oancf/lt are highly correlated the reweighting is unlikely to produce economically distinct information.

Swapping the investment leg from a capital-intensity level to gross-PP&E growth while holding the archive's cash-coverage leg fixed is a legitimate, well-motivated flow-vs-level ablation, though it retains half of an already-tested signal and the growth leg overlaps heavily with the published asset-growth/investment anomaly.

critic_notes.target_name: Harvesting Old Assets With Strong Cash Flow
critic_notes.rationale: Asset age (ppent/ppegt) is a genuinely new state variable here and the expression matches the stated hypothesis, but the construct is close to the intersection of two published factors (low investment/CMA and cash-based profitability/RMW), so any FF5 alpha must be shown to survive the profitability leg standing alone.

critic_notes.target_name: Operating Capital Bloat Without Cash Conversion
critic_notes.rationale: The two legs are not economically orthogonal — low asset turnover and weak cash-flow-on-assets are both proxies for the same operating-efficiency dimension — so the product is close to a monotone restatement of poor profitability rather than a true conditional interaction, and it reuses the exact cash-flow leg of the already-evaluated intangibles signal.

critic_notes.target_name: Disciplined Capex Retrenchment by Profitable Firms
critic_notes.rationale: Both legs are direct restatements of published anomalies (Titman-Wei-Xie capital investment growth and ROA/profitability), so the signal is essentially the double-sort intersection of two known factors with no new economic content beyond their product.

Conditioning capacity expansion on the second derivative of revenue growth is a timing-mismatch mechanism not present in the archive and not spanned by level-based investment or profitability factors, the expression is internally consistent with the negative expected sign, and coverage should be adequate — the main risk is noise in the two-step sales-acceleration term.

The added leverage leg is largely collinear with the intangible leg (goodwill is typically debt-funded) and, combined with weak cash flow, mainly re-expresses the well-documented distress/leverage-times-low-profitability effect, so this reads as an incremental amplification of the archive's existing intangible signal rather than a new mechanism.

Maturity mismatch (dlc/act) is a genuinely distinct conditioning variable from the archive's cash-flow coverage screen, the mechanism is coherent, the sign follows naturally from the expression, and the industry-ranked investment leg guards against an industry-capital-intensity artifact.

The real-options framing is coherent and the second-moment conditioning leg is new to this archive, but both legs are individually known negative return predictors (investment anomaly, fundamental/cash-flow volatility), so a negative result may simply compound two published effects rather than demonstrate a true interaction — and the 5-year VOL will thin coverage.

Low capx/dp is close to mechanically redundant with a heavily depreciated net-to-gross PP&E ratio (sub-replacement spending is precisely what ages the asset base), so the third leg mostly re-weights the same tilt, and the resulting low-investment × high-cash-profitability portfolio is largely spanned by CMA and RMW in the very FF5 benchmark being used.

The expected positive sign is fitted post hoc to one prior wrong-signed alpha and sits in tension with the expression's own asset-growth leg (high PP&E growth is a canonical negative predictor), leaving the composite's direction likely determined by the known cash-profitability leg rather than by the stated countercyclical-conviction mechanism.

A well-motivated, internally consistent leg-swap ablation that directly tests whether the prior inventory signal's missing FMB slope came from a factor-loaded conditioning variable, and it is diagnostic either way — though the inventory-growth-minus-sales-growth base is itself a published anomaly, so any result must be shown incremental to it.

This is a mechanical ensemble average of the archive's two existing capex×fragility signals rather than a new mechanism, so any gain in t-stats will come from noise-diversification within an already-tested construct, not from new economic content.

critic_notes.target_name: Heavy Capex After No Earnings Payoff
critic_notes.rationale: A realized return-on-incremental-investment conditioner is a genuinely new and well-deflated quality gauge whose sign logic matches the expression, though the NEG(ΔIB) component embeds a known earnings-change/earnings-momentum main effect that should be diagnosed if the signal works.

The stated purpose — stripping the conditioner's main effect — is not what the expression does, since masking growers to zero pins them at one extreme of the intangible-rank scale and thereby hard-codes an even stronger sales-growth main effect, on top of the signal being a re-parameterization of the archive's gen-3 intangibles-versus-sales signal.

Swapping the harvesting family's cash-profitability conditioner for a cash-to-current-liabilities conditioner is a defensible attempt to escape RMW/CMA spanning and is internally consistent, but the cash-holdings main effect is itself a documented anomaly and the asset-age leg is recycled, so the incremental content is modest.

Extending the maturity-mismatch conditioner from capital to labor commitments is a legitimate mechanism-level generalization with a coherent sign, though both legs (hiring rate, short-debt/liquidity) are individually published anomalies and emp growth is coarse and noisily reported.

The diagnostic motivation of isolating which leg failed is reasonable, but the construct is a straight rank-product crossover of two already-tested archive legs and closely tracks the known investment×financial-constraints/RE-lifecycle result, with the strong low-RE distress main effect likely to dominate.

critic_notes.target_name: Capex Against Net Short-Term Funding Position
critic_notes.rationale: The expression is internally consistent (heavy capex × negative net near-term liquidity → low returns) and netting cash against short debt firm-by-firm is a defensible economic re-specification rather than a rank average, but it remains a conditioner swap within the already-productive capx/ppent × short-funding family, so the incremental information is modest.

This is essentially the mirrored corner of the archive's accepted "Aged Capital With Liquidity Firepower" using the identical two state variables with both legs sign-flipped — the non-symmetry of the rank product makes it technically a different portfolio but not a substantively new mechanism, and the young-PP&E leg is largely a proxy for recent asset growth, so a negative result would be uninformative and a positive one near-redundant.

critic_notes.target_name: Capital Deepening Backed by Cash Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: Capital-for-labor substitution is a genuinely new construct here and the netting of headcount growth is a real design choice, but the expected positive sign sits in direct tension with the natural direction of the dominant leg (gross PP&E growth is a well-documented negative predictor, as the archive's own ppegt-growth signals confirm), so the sign prior is fragile and rests entirely on the emp subtraction and the coverage conditioner.

The first leg is close to a direct rediscovery of the published net-debt-issuance/liability-growth anomaly (and overlaps the archive's GROWTH(lt) − GROWTH(ppegt) signal), while the second leg (capx/depreciation, already tested at ~zero) carries a natural direction opposite to the expected positive sign, so the proposal mixes a known effect with a leg whose sign prior contradicts the hypothesis.

The diagnosis of why the gen-3 intangibles signal had an inverted FMB slope (a contrarian sales-growth conditioner) is sound and the replacement conditioner is correctly signed, but the result is a two-deflator re-specification of the gen-1 intangibles × weak-cash-flow signal that already delivered −4.7% alpha at t = −3.9, so it risks being a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Investment at Own-History Peak Without Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: This is the gen-1 "Capex Without Debt-Service Capacity" signal with a single operator swapped (IND_RANK → TS_RANK over five annual observations), i.e., a minimal variant whose within-firm leg is also coarsely discretized at annual frequency, so it is too incremental to justify a separate test slot despite the legitimate underlying design question.

This is the archive champion ("Overpaid Intangibles Without Cash Coverage") with `intan` swapped for `gdwl`, a subset of the same balance-sheet line, so it is a component-decomposition diagnostic rather than a new signal and will be highly correlated with the existing result (goodwill typically dominates intan for the acquisitive firms that drive the short leg).

critic_notes.target_name: Overpaid Intangibles Against Net Funding Position
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible recombination — it keeps the slope-carrying overpayment leg and substitutes a stock-liquidity conditioner for the flow-coverage one, which is a genuinely different economic state — but it is still a two-leg swap between existing archive components, so novelty is modest and there is a real risk it simply inherits the net-funding leg's alpha-without-slope profile.

critic_notes.target_name: Expansion With Stretched Depreciation and No Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: Two problems: the base signal's legs are mechanically confounded (rapid `ppegt` growth mechanically depresses `dp/ppegt` because new assets are only partially depreciated in year one, so "stretched useful lives" is not identified), and bolting the heavily reused cash-coverage rank onto it as a third multiplicative term is an incremental augmentation whose triple-rank product concentrates on a thin joint tail rather than a substantively different mechanism.

The wedge construct is the same family as the archive's gen-4 "Obligations Outgrowing Productive Capacity" (X-growth minus `ppegt` growth) with `at` substituted for `lt`, and the leading term is dominated by the well-known asset-growth anomaly already spanned by FF5's CMA, so both the novelty and the expected incremental alpha are low.

critic_notes.target_name: Aged Capital With Net Cash Position
critic_notes.rationale: This is the gen-4 "Aged Capital With Liquidity Firepower" signal with `che` replaced by `che - dlc` in the same numerator over the same denominator — precisely the single-term deflator tweak the reasoning preemptively disclaims — and it is unlikely to produce evidence distinguishable from the existing result.

The acquisition-share-of-investment mix is the only genuinely new construct in this batch and is economically well motivated, but the stated fix is wrong — every non-acquirer still maps to exactly 0, so the zero mass point that crippled the gen-0 signal survives, and the denominator is unstable for firms with negligible total investment.

critic_notes.target_name: Purchased Growth Stock and Flow Without Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: This is a compensatory average (SUMRANK) of the two highest-scoring archive signals' investment legs bolted to their shared conditioner, so it is largely a blend of already-tested results rather than a new mechanism — and the stated logic ("requires both the history and the ongoing behavior to agree") contradicts what SUMRANK computes, since a high rank on one leg fully offsets a low rank on the other.

The lumpiness/zero-mass argument is a legitimate measurement fix, but a five-year window on the identical numerator, denominator and conditioner as the gen-6 "Bought Growth Rather Than Built" signal is a horizon variant that will be highly correlated with it and adds no new economic content beyond "persistence."

The construct is genuinely new to the archive, but DELTA(intan) minus aqc does not isolate internally capitalized soft costs as claimed — intan (which includes goodwill in Compustat) is simultaneously reduced by amortization/impairment and inflated by stock-financed acquisitions whose cash outlay never enters aqc, so the top tail will be dominated by equity-funded acquirers rather than aggressive capitalizers, breaking the hypothesis-expression link.

critic_notes.target_name: Soft Assets Exceeding Book Equity Without Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: Negative tangible book scaled by assets is an economically distinct statement from the champion's intangibles-per-revenue-dollar and is correctly constructed to avoid a negative-equity denominator, though the leg decomposes into intangible intensity plus book leverage and, interacted with a cash-flow-coverage conditioner, risks collapsing into the well-known distress/leverage channel rather than an impairment channel.

critic_notes.target_name: Purchased Growth With a Write-Down Record
critic_notes.rationale: The conditioner is mismeasured for the stated mechanism: ni − ib captures extraordinary items and discontinued operations, not impairments and restructuring charges (which sit in special items above the ib line and are largely absent from this gap, especially post-2002), so the "write-down record" interpretation does not match what the expression computes and the sparse, near-zero variable likely explains the earlier wrong-signed alpha the proposal is trying to diagnose.

critic_notes.target_name: Capacity Growth Funded by Cumulative Free Cash
critic_notes.rationale: The surplus-side test is economically coherent and motivated by two complementary archive results, but the claim that "the interaction is the entire content" is overstated — a product of two [0,1] ranks retains strong main effects, so the long leg may substantially reflect a plain cumulative-FCF/profitability tilt that FF5's RMW absorbs.

critic_notes.target_name: Marginal Cash Return on the Investment Program
critic_notes.rationale: A genuinely distinct construct — marginal rather than level cash productivity of capital, with a lag structure matched to project horizons and a sign convention consistent with the archive's Low-CROIC precedent — though the reviewer should watch that the small-denominator (low cumulative capex) tail does not turn the cross-sectional sort into a capital-intensity sort despite the 1% winsorization.

This is the gen-7 "Capacity Growth Funded by Cumulative Free Cash" signal with the same two cumulative quantities recombined as a ratio instead of an asset-scaled difference — a deflator/functional-form swap on the conditioner rather than a substantively different mechanism, and its rank transform will leave it highly correlated with the tested version.

Because both legs are bounded ranks, this signal is mechanically approximately RANK(coverage) minus the already-tested gen-2 signal, so a negative slope would be driven mostly by the weak-cash-coverage main effect (a known distress/profitability effect) rather than by disinvestment, and the stated hypothesis also runs against the documented asset-growth direction; it has diagnostic value but is not a clean alpha candidate.

critic_notes.target_name: Purchased Base With Debt Coming Due
critic_notes.rationale: The intangible-load × short-maturity-debt pairing is untested and the refinancing channel is economically separable from the cash-coverage channel, but this is now the third conditioner swapped onto the same intangibles-per-sales leg, so the incremental information over the existing champion is likely modest and should be assessed against a correlation with it.

critic_notes.target_name: Conjunctive Screen on Overpayment and Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: Replacing MUL with MIN on the champion's identical two legs is an aggregation-operator variant of an already-evaluated signal; the conjunction-versus-main-effect question is legitimate but would be answered more informatively by explicitly decomposing the champion (e.g., double sorts or leg-wise controls) than by re-running a near-duplicate composite.

Negating both legs of the tested gen-3 inventory-bloat signal yields a construct dominated by the two legs' main effects — the well-documented inventory-growth/accrual anomaly and the cash-flow-profitability effect — so a positive result would largely be a rediscovery of published anomalies rather than evidence for the claimed destocking-quality interaction.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash Cover of Purchased Base and Claims
critic_notes.rationale: The denominator incoherently sums an asset (intan) with total claims (lt) that partly finance it, and since lt dominates intan for most firms the signal collapses to cash-flow-to-total-debt — a standard coverage/distress measure already exercised in this archive via oancf/lt and Low CROIC, so it is a near-cosmetic hybrid of two tested signals rather than a new economic quantity.

critic_notes.target_name: Growth Funded by Surplus Against Claims
critic_notes.rationale: This is a pure denominator swap (at → lt) on the archive's best long-side signal with an otherwise identical construction, and the two scalings will produce highly correlated ranks, so it is the kind of cosmetic variant the objective explicitly discourages rather than a substantively different mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Serial Buyers of Growth Without Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: MIN over the investment legs of two already-tested archive signals that share the identical conditioner is an ensemble of known results rather than a new hypothesis, and its short tail is by construction the intersection of two portfolios already shown to deliver ~-5.5% to -6% alpha, so incremental information is likely near zero.

The intangible-load × accrual-quality pairing is internally consistent and is the one quality dimension not yet crossed with this family, but the accrual leg is the Sloan cash-flow accrual measure (already present in inverted form in the gen-2 signal), so the test must show the interaction adds beyond the standalone accrual anomaly.

critic_notes.target_name: Sub-Replacement Spending With Claims Well Covered
critic_notes.rationale: The flow-based harvest measure (capx vs depreciation) is a genuinely different construction from the earlier stock-based asset-age signals and is motivated by an observed sign reversal, but low investment × high cash-flow coverage risks being largely the CMA and RMW main effects recombined, so the FF5 alpha rather than the raw spread will be the decisive evidence.

critic_notes.target_name: Acquisitions Funded With New Long-Term Debt
critic_notes.rationale: Source-of-funds for the acquisition is a separable channel absent from the archive and the two contemporaneous legs coherently describe one financing decision, though the large tied mass of zero-aqc firms will make the long leg uninformative and the debt-issuance leg alone is a known external-financing anomaly that must be controlled for.
